# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 62

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 62:1 "destroyed" vs. "perishes" — treatment of body loss

- **EMET:** "why the flesh is destroyed when the soul is saved"
- **LOGOS:** "why the flesh is destroyed when the soul is saved"
- **PNEUMA:** "why the flesh perishes while the soul is saved"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "why the flesh is destroyed when the soul is saved." The passive "is destroyed" rather than "perishes" preserves the sense of external judgment.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 62:1 "kept their spirit pure" vs. "kept their spirit pure from the beginning"

- **EMET:** "kept their spirit pure from the beginning"
- **LOGOS:** "kept their spirit pure from the beginning"
- **PNEUMA:** "kept their spirit pure from the very beginning"
- **Note:** All three agree; PNEUMA adds "very" for emphasis.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "kept their spirit pure from the beginning." The phrase "from the beginning" (*ap' archēs*) is present in the Greek; PNEUMA's "very" is acceptable emphasis.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 62:2 "the life they shall live will be shorter" vs. "somewhat shorter"

- **EMET:** "the life they shall live will be shorter"
- **LOGOS:** "the life they shall live will be somewhat shorter"
- **PNEUMA:** "their life will be somewhat shorter"
- **Greek:** *hē zōē autōn oligōtera estin* — their life is less/somewhat less
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the life they shall live will be somewhat shorter" (LOGOS). *Oligōteros* = comparative of *oligos* (few/little); "somewhat shorter" captures the comparative.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 62:2 "incurs his own loss" vs. "brings the loss on themselves"

- **EMET:** "undertakes his loss himself"
- **LOGOS:** "incurs his own loss"
- **PNEUMA:** "they bring the loss on themselves"
- **Greek:** *blabēn heautō perioieitai* — he acquires harm/loss for himself
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "incurs his own loss" (LOGOS). "Incurs" is the precise legal/commercial term for acquiring liability; EMET's "undertakes" is awkward.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 62:3 "to go away from God" vs. "to depart from God"

- **EMET:** "to go away from God is to defile the flesh"
- **LOGOS:** "to depart from God is to defile the flesh"
- **PNEUMA:** "Departing from God is what defiles the flesh"
- **Greek:** *apochorein apo tou theou miasmos estin* — departing from God is defilement
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "to depart from God is to defile the flesh" (LOGOS). "Depart" (*apochorein*) implies a deliberate movement away; "go away" is vaguer.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 62:3 "associates with the deeds of the double-minded" vs. "involved in the behavior of double-minded people"

- **EMET:** "any man who associates with the deeds of the double-minded"
- **LOGOS:** "any person who associates with the deeds of the double-minded"
- **PNEUMA:** "anyone who gets involved in the behavior of double-minded people"
- **Greek:** *koinōnei tais praxesin tōn dipsychōn* — participates/partners with the deeds of the double-minded
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "any person who associates with the deeds of the double-minded" (LOGOS). "Associates" captures *koinōnein* (to share in, participate); PNEUMA's "gets involved in" is slightly too casual.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 62:4 "deceive themselves with their knowledge" vs. "with their so-called knowledge"

- **EMET:** "deceive themselves with their knowledge"
- **LOGOS:** "deceive themselves with their so-called knowledge"
- **PNEUMA:** "deceive themselves through their supposed knowledge"
- **Greek:** *apatōntes heautous en tē gnōsei autōn* — deceiving themselves in their knowledge
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "deceive themselves with their so-called knowledge" (LOGOS). The context implies false or insufficient knowledge; "so-called" makes the irony explicit. EMET loses this irony.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 62:5 "called by the name of God" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "called by the name of God"
- **LOGOS:** "called by the name of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "called by God's name"
- **Note:** All three agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "called by the name of God" (EMET/LOGOS). The phrase *onomazomenoi* (bearing the name/being named) has baptismal resonance — these are baptized Christians.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 62:5 "vanity of this world" vs. "emptiness of this world"

- **EMET:** "the vanity of this world"
- **LOGOS:** "the vanity of this world"
- **PNEUMA:** "the emptiness of this world"
- **Greek:** *hē mataiotes tou aiōnos toutou* — the vanity/emptiness of this age
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the vanity of this world." EMET and LOGOS agree; *mataiotes* = vanity/emptiness (cf. Eccl 1:2 LXX); "vanity" preserves the classical biblical resonance.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 62.*
